data.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** b0db086932ab73cf3e9bdf1c0fa03e2d0612ae00
* **branch:** feat/coderabbit-defense-and-timeout-20260512-173056
* **PR created:** https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/107
* **caller:** orchestrator session running COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md then `merge-to-main.sh`
* **merge.strategy:** pr
* **enforcement.strategy:** ci

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

After `merge-to-main.sh` pushes the branch and creates a PR via `gh pr create`, the post-PR finalize phase should only invoke LLM thread resolution when there are actually unresolved PR review threads to resolve. On a freshly created PR — before CI has run and before any reviewer (human, CodeRabbit, or llm-review) has filed a comment — the unresolved-threads set is empty. With nothing to resolve, the pipeline has a valid path forward: either skip the resolve_threads phase entirely and proceed to the wait-for-checks / merge phase, or exit cleanly with "PR open, awaiting CI" status.

The current behavior creates friction and agent confusion: a fresh PR with no threads cannot be "resolved" by any dispatch, yet the script demands a dispatch be configured and emits an escalation when one is not. The escalation pushes work back onto the calling session agent for a problem (no threads) that requires no work.

#### Actual Behavior

`merge-to-main.sh` succeeded through push and PR creation (PR #107), then emitted this structured escalation as its final output and exited:

```
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "escalation": "local_no_llm_dispatch",
  "phase": "resolve_threads",
  "reason": "_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD not set; cannot dispatch LLM thread resolution locally (PR: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/107; unresolved: )",
  "instructions": "Session agent must resolve the open PR review threads manually. Read ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/workflows/PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md and drive the loop via pr-finalize-classify.sh, then re-run merge-to-main.sh.",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-13T01:54:58Z"
}
```

Key observation: the `reason` field shows `unresolved: ` (empty string after the colon) — the script knows there are zero unresolved threads, but still escalates because `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` is unset. The unconditional escalation conflates two distinct conditions:

1. Dispatch environment is unconfigured (LLM dispatch command missing).
2. There is work to be dispatched (≥1 unresolved thread).

Only condition 2 should trigger session-agent escalation. Condition 1 alone, with an empty thread set, has no work to do — the correct behavior is to short-circuit past resolve_threads and continue.

#### Friction caused

- The session agent must read PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md and `pr-finalize-classify.sh` to confirm there are no threads to resolve — work the script already knows is unnecessary.
- The "valid path forward" (`merge-to-main.sh --resume` once CI passes) is not communicated by the escalation JSON; the instructions imply manual thread resolution is required.
- For autonomous sessions without a dispatch command configured (the common local-dev case), every PR-strategy merge ends with this escalation regardless of whether threads exist, training the agent to ignore the message and inflating cognitive load on every merge.

### 3. Action History

1. Made surgical edits to fix-bug skill (10 files).
2. Ran COMMIT-WORKFLOW.md inline: pre-flight, skip-review-check (script not found, ignored — separate issue), enforcement.strategy=ci → emitted .skipped markers, staged with `git add -u`, committed (`2b33b900c2`), emitted commit-workflow start/end events.
3. Ran `.claude/scripts/dso merge-to-main.sh`. Pipeline: merged origin/main into branch, ran pre-push lint + sprint-trailer hooks (Passed), pushed branch, called `gh pr create` → PR #107 created and reported.
4. Pipeline emitted the escalation JSON above and exited with the resolve_threads escalation as the final state — even though `unresolved: ` was empty in the same JSON.
5. PR #107 status verified via `gh pr view 107`: state=OPEN, mergeable=MERGEABLE, 11 checks IN_PROGRESS, 1 check COMPLETED/SUCCESS — confirming there is no review-thread work yet (and may never be, if all checks pass and no human review is required).

### 4. Chronological Rationalization

This is not a regression of a previously working behavior — it is a design gap in the resolve_threads phase: the precondition check is `dispatch_cmd_set?` when it should be `(dispatch_cmd_set AND unresolved_threads > 0) OR unresolved_threads == 0 → skip`. The empty-set short-circuit was likely never implemented because in the original PR-finalize design, the script was expected to wait for CodeRabbit / llm-review threads to land before checking — but with `merge.strategy=pr` and a freshly opened PR, the check fires immediately on a known-empty set.

### 5. Skills and Workflows

* `plugins/dso/docs/workflows/PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md` (referenced by the escalation instructions)
* `plugins/dso/scripts/pr-finalize-classify.sh` (driver script the escalation directs the agent to use)
* `plugins/dso/scripts/merge-to-main.sh` (calls the resolve_threads phase that emits the escalation)
* The emitter is in `plugins/dso/scripts/` — exact file TBD; locate via `grep -rn "local_no_llm_dispatch" plugins/dso/`

### 6. Logs

Final lines of `merge-to-main.sh` stdout, captured 2026-05-13T01:54:58Z:

```
INFO: Created PR #107: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/107
{"schema_version": 1, "escalation": "local_no_llm_dispatch", "phase": "resolve_threads", "reason": "_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD not set; cannot dispatch LLM thread resolution locally (PR: https://github.com/navapbc/digital-service-orchestra/pull/107; unresolved: )", "instructions": "Session agent must resolve the open PR review threads manually. Read ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/docs/workflows/PR-FINALIZE-WORKFLOW.md and drive the loop via pr-finalize-classify.sh, then re-run merge-to-main.sh.", "timestamp": "2026-05-13T01:54:58Z"}
```

#### Suggested fix shape (informational only — Zero Inference applies; treat as a starting point for investigation, not a prescribed cause)

In the resolve_threads phase, gate the escalation on `unresolved_thread_count > 0`. When the count is zero, log a single-line INFO "no unresolved threads; resolve_threads phase short-circuited" and continue to the next phase (wait-for-checks / merge / report-pending). Only when count > 0 AND `_LLM_DISPATCH_CMD` is unset should the script emit the `local_no_llm_dispatch` escalation.
data.title: [merge-to-main]: fresh PR with zero unresolved threads -> escalates local_no_llm_dispatch instead of completing
